raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 MegaMoE decode and verify spend several launches on the gate GEMM, the sqrtsoftplus top-k and the routing copy; DeepGEMM's `bf16_mega_gate` does this in one kernel.

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_GATE` routes MegaMoE decode/verify (up to 2048 rows) through `bf16_mega_gate`, including vision-biased and hash-routed layers and the padded-row mask.
- Unless routed experts are being captured, the gate writes straight into MegaMoE's routing buffer and the pre-dispatch only quantizes (`kCopyTopk`). EPLB static and dynamic placements are applied in-kernel via `to_physical_map`/`logical_count` (dynamic spreads replicas by rank and token instead of `randint`), and the expert distribution recorder reads the buffer. `lp`/`fake` dispatch falls back to the regular router.
- `SGLANG_SIMULATE_*` keeps the gate on: the balanced override runs after it, masking padded rows and applying the routed scale in its one launch.
- Tests: `test_mega_gate.py` (kernel vs reference under CUDA graph replay), a masked/scaled case in `test_round_robin_ep_balance.py`, and MegaGate unit tests in `test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py`.

Setup: the CI `test_deepseek_v41_flash_gb300_dp4ep4` recipe (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, `--attn-dp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --enable-dp-lm-head`, DSPARK block 5, breakable prefill graphs) with `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` instead of `none`, `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8192`, sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.3 from the `nightly-dev-cu13-20261019` image. Same evaluator settings as CI: sgl-eval GSM8K 200 examples (`temperature 0`, `max_tokens 4096`, threshold 0.95) and MMMU-Pro 200 examples (`temperature 1.0`, thinking, `max_tokens 32768`, threshold 0.75), plus the DSPARK acceptance assert.

| `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_GATE` | GSM8K | accept len (GSM8K) | MMMU-Pro | accept len (MMMU-Pro) | result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 0.980 | 4.27 | 0.780 | 3.24 | OK, exit 0 |
| 1 | 0.980 | 4.41 | 0.795 | 3.29 | OK, exit 0 |

MMMU-Pro samples at temperature 1.0, so the 0.015 gap is within run noise. The gate-on run JIT-built four new `sm100_bf16_mega_gate` DeepGEMM variants during its window and the gate-off run built none, so the fused path was exercised on every decode and verify step. Not covered here: EPLB (the in-kernel remap path), hash layers under EPLB, and `SGLANG_SIMULATE_*`.

detail.body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 MegaMoE decode and verify spend several launches on the gate GEMM, the sqrtsoftplus top-k and the routing copy; DeepGEMM's `bf16_mega_gate` does this in one kernel.

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_GATE` routes MegaMoE decode/verify (up to 2048 rows) through `bf16_mega_gate`, including vision-biased and hash-routed layers and the padded-row mask.
- Unless routed experts are being captured, the gate writes straight into MegaMoE's routing buffer and the pre-dispatch only quantizes (`kCopyTopk`). EPLB static and dynamic placements are applied in-kernel via `to_physical_map`/`logical_count` (dynamic spreads replicas by rank and token instead of `randint`), and the expert distribution recorder reads the buffer. `lp`/`fake` dispatch falls back to the regular router.
- `SGLANG_SIMULATE_*` keeps the gate on: the balanced override runs after it, masking padded rows and applying the routed scale in its one launch.
- Tests: `test_mega_gate.py` (kernel vs reference under CUDA graph replay), a masked/scaled case in `test_round_robin_ep_balance.py`, and MegaGate unit tests in `test_mega_moe_deepgemm_api.py`.
